newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African human rights team to visit Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: African human rights team to visit Nigeria.

text.p: An African human rights team will visit Nigeria this week to investigate, a week after United Nations envoys cancelled a similar mission, local rights activists said on Wednesday.
"They have been trying to come for almost a year," Abdul Oroh, executive director of the Civil Liberties Organisation (CLO), the leading human rights group in Nigeria, told Reuters.
The U.N. mission called off a visit last week after the military government refused them access to jails and detainees.

Oroh and local newspapers said the government had agreed to allow the African team to see detainees including presidential claimant Moshood Abiola, 19 youths from the Ogoni minority tribe detained over the 1994 murder of four Ogoni chiefs, as well as human rights groups.
"The government probably wants to use the visit to counter whatever the U.N. people will write about Nigeria," Oroh said.

The Ogoni youths face the death penalty like executed author Ken Saro-Wiwa, who was hanged with eight other Ogoni minority rights activists in 1995 over the same murders after a trial condemned internationally as unfair.
The U.N. mission had been due to report to the U.N. Human Rights Commission, which opens its annual session on March 10 when Nigeria is expected to be in the dock for rights abuses.
The three-man mission expected to arrive on Friday is from the African Commission on Human Rights and Peoples' Rights.

It includes former Togolese minister Koffi Amega, who led a mission to Nigeria last year from former U.N. Secretary-General Boutrous Boutrous-Ghali, which endorsed the military's programme for transition to civil rule.
The CLO and the Constitutional Rights Project, another Nigerian human rights group, in a joint letter to the mission members, protested against the inclusion of Amega.
"We are concerned that Mr Koffi Amega's inclusion in the mission already taints its objectivity," said their letter, which was released to the media.

The mission lasts until March 14, the day before local council polls that are expected to test how seriously the military government is committed to handing power to an elected president next year as it has promised.
